policy: Each record below was normalized from authoritative publisher, PubMed, or equivalent bibliographic metadata. No guessed fields are permitted.

records.citation: Shannon, Claude E. 1949. ‘Communication in the Presence of Noise.’ Proceedings of the IRE 37 (1): 10–21. https://doi.org/10.1109/JRPROC.1949.232969.
records.claimBurden: Sampling interval and temporal resolution can determine whether a time-varying signal is recoverable from observations. This is a signal-processing authority, not evidence of biological agency.

records.citation: West, Geoffrey B., and James H. Brown. 2005. ‘The Origin of Allometric Scaling Laws in Biology from Genomes to Ecosystems: Towards a Quantitative Unifying Theory of Biological Structure and Organization.’ Journal of Experimental Biology 208 (9): 1575–1592. https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.01589.
records.claimBurden: Many biological rates and characteristic quantities vary systematically with organism size; scale changes can therefore alter the time window at which a process becomes visible. No universal exponent is asserted.

records.citation: Clutton-Brock, Tim, and Ben C. Sheldon. 2010. ‘Individuals and Populations: The Role of Long-Term, Individual-Based Studies of Animals in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology.’ Trends in Ecology & Evolution 25 (10): 562–573. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tree.2010.08.002.
records.claimBurden: Ecological and evolutionary processes may require observation over years or decades; short observation windows can fail to reveal important dynamics.

records.citation: Rainey, Paul B., and Silvia De Monte. 2014. ‘Resolving Conflicts During the Evolutionary Transition to Multicellular Life.’ Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics 45: 599–620. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-ecolsys-120213-091740.
records.claimBurden: Multicellular individuality depends not merely on cooperation but on mechanisms that mediate or suppress conflict among lower-level units.

records.citation: Turing, A. M. 1952. ‘The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis.’ Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological Sciences 237 (641): 37–72. https://doi.org/10.1098/rstb.1952.0012.
records.claimBurden: Reaction-diffusion is a mathematically explicit mechanism class by which initially homogeneous systems can generate spatial pattern. It is not presented as the sole mechanism of morphogenesis.

records.citation: Milinkovitch, Michel C., Ebrahim Jahanbakhsh, and Szabolcs Zakany. 2023. ‘The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reaction Diffusion in Vertebrate Skin Color Patterning.’ Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology 39: 145–174. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-cellbio-120319-024414.
records.claimBurden: Modern review support for reaction-diffusion as a useful and empirically relevant patterning framework in vertebrate skin, while preserving the chapter’s caution that development is mechanistically plural.
